body:
On platforms that Lightning CSS has no native package for, such as Linux on ppc64le and s390x, `vite build` fails because Vite can't load Lightning CSS, which minifies CSS by default:

```
[lightningcss minify] Cannot find module '../lightningcss.linux-ppc64-gnu.node'
```

`lightningcss-wasm` is an optional peer dependency with the same API in Node.
Overlapping calls to its `bundleAsync` break each other, for example by returning another file's CSS, so Vite runs those calls one at a time when it uses `lightningcss-wasm`.

Setting `build.cssMinify: 'esbuild'` avoids Lightning CSS only for minification; with `css.transformer: 'lightningcss'`, Vite needs Lightning CSS itself.
parcel-bundler/lightningcss#1217 would add native packages for ppc64le and s390x, but it has had no review since it opened in April, and the fallback also applies to other platforms without a native package, such as OpenHarmony (parcel-bundler/lightningcss#1285).

With `lightningcss-wasm` and `css.transformer: 'lightningcss'`, CSS module class names depend on the project's absolute path, because `lightningcss-wasm` ignores `projectRoot`.
On s390x, `lightningcss-wasm` fails (devongovett/napi-wasm#8).

fixes #23955
title: feat(css): fall back to `lightningcss-wasm` when the native package can't be loaded

## Problem

After an HMR update reaches a self-accepting boundary, importer modules can still receive updated HMR timestamps even though their existing instances remain active in the browser.

A subsequent lazy import may then load the same importer under a different timestamped URL, causing duplicate module evaluation, inconsistent singleton identity, and repeated side effects.

## Changes

- Prevent unnecessary HMR timestamp propagation beyond self-accepting boundaries.
- Preserve transform invalidation to ensure updated dependencies are referenced correctly.
- Handle shared importers reached through multiple dependency paths, including traversal-order edge cases.
- Add regression coverage for module identity, evaluation counts, and HMR invalidation behavior.

The fix introduces no new dependencies or public API changes.

## Validation

The browser regression reproduced 2 module evaluations before the fix and 1 afterward, with singleton identity preserved.

Reported final validation:

- 1,110 unit tests passed.
- 238 broader browser tests passed.
- 128 targeted HMR/reload tests passed.
- 66 bundled-development tests passed.
- 38 production-build tests passed.
- Build, type checking, lint, formatting, and commit hooks passed.

An earlier intermittent extra-transform failure in an existing soft-invalidation test was not reproduced in 20 repeated runs on either the patched or upstream implementation. Its cause remains undetermined.

## AI Assistance and Review

AI assistance was used for code investigation, implementation, and test development.

## Personal Review

I reviewed the changes to `moduleGraph.ts` and the regression tests, focusing on HMR timestamp propagation across self-accepting boundaries, preservation of transform invalidation, and handling of shared importer paths.

The browser regression reproduced two module evaluations before the fix and one afterward, with singleton identity preserved. The reported unit, integration, browser, and build checks passed.

An intermittent extra-transform failure in the existing soft-invalidation test could not be reproduced during follow-up testing. Its root cause remains undetermined.

## Related Issue

Fixes #23942

body:
fixes #23894

So here's the bug: if the module that starts a nested worker gets tree-shaken out of the main bundle, but another worker still uses it, the outer worker ends up pointing at the nested worker's file, and that file just isn't there.

What happens is the main build sees the `new Worker(new URL(...))` call and emits the nested worker early (`generateEntryUrlExpr`). Then `generateBundle` sees the module got tree-shaken, decides the worker is dead, and deletes it. Then it realises the worker is actually still needed and tries to emit it again, but Rolldown ignores a second `emitFile` for the same file. So it's gone.

The fix: figure out what's still live first, and don't delete anything that's still used through another worker. Nothing that's still needed gets deleted, so nothing needs re-adding.

For the test, the main page imports a module without using it, and a live worker uses that same module to start a nested worker. The test checks the nested worker's file exists. It fails without the fix and passes with it. A nested worker nobody uses still gets removed like before. I also ran the worker playground in dev, build and bundled-dev modes, plus the `packages/vite` unit tests.

I thought about ripping out the whole emit-early-then-delete thing, but kept the change small instead. One thing to look at: the same cleanup runs inside worker sub-builds, so those now keep live nested workers too.

There was an earlier PR for this, vitejs/vite#23899, but its author closed it to cut down on open PRs. It takes a similar approach, keeping still-live workers in both main and worker builds.

AI usage: Claude Code helped me with testing and information gathering. I built the issue's repro with and without the fix and checked that the nested worker was referenced but missing before, and emitted after.
title: fix(worker): keep nested workers still used by a live worker

### What is this PR solving?

On the documentation sidebar, hovering over the ViteConf tag caused an infinite flicker/resize loop at the bottom edge.

This occurred because `.viteconf:hover` used `--vp-c-brand-light` and `.heading` used `--vp-c-brand-lighter`, both of which are undefined in `@voidzero-dev/vitepress-theme`. In CSS, referencing an undefined variable in a shorthand declaration (`border: 2px solid var(--vp-c-brand-light)`) causes the entire declaration to be treated as unset at computed-value time, collapsing the border to 0px and shrinking the tag's height by 4px on hover.

This PR updates the hover state to `border-color: var(--vp-c-brand-1)` (preserving the 2px border width set on `.viteconf`) and updates `.heading` to use `var(--vp-c-brand-1)`.

### Related issue

fixes #23905

### Validation

- Verified locally with Playwright and a preview build of `docs/.vitepress/dist`:
  - Before: element height shrank from 69.56px to 65.56px on hover, causing boundary oscillation when the cursor was near the bottom edge.
  - After: height remains constant at 69.56px (0px delta), border transitions to brand color smoothly, and hover stays stable.
- `pnpm run docs-build` passes.
- `oxlint .` passes.

AI assistance was used to help inspect computed styles and test the hover behavior. I verified the CSS variable resolution and confirmed the fix locally.

## Summary

`reloadModule()` called while a transform of the same module is still running leaves the module serving the old code. The HMR fetch that follows joins the in-flight transform, and its result is cached as `transformResult`, so later requests get stale code too.

## Root Cause

The race guards in `transformRequest` and `loadAndTransform` compare against `lastInvalidationTimestamp`. File changes set it through `moduleGraph.onFileChange`. `reloadModule()` only goes through `updateModules`, which invalidates with `isHmr = true` and sets `lastHMRTimestamp` instead. So the guards never see the reload.

## Changes

- `DevEnvironment.reloadModule` invalidates the module through `moduleGraph.invalidateModule()` before running the HMR update, the same way a file change does.
- The deprecated `server.reloadModule` gets the same change.
- New test in `server/__tests__/hmr.spec.ts`. It holds a virtual module's transform open across a `reloadModule()` call and checks that the new code is served and cached.

## Testing

- The new unit test fails on `main` and passes with this change.
- `pnpm test-unit`, `pnpm test-serve hmr hmr-ssr`, `pnpm run typecheck` and `pnpm run lint` pass.
- The repro from the issue goes from 5/5 stale runs to 0/20.

## Manual Verification

1. Build Vite and run the repro script from #23941 against the local build with `RUNS=20`.
2. Every run serves `v2` for both the last HMR fetch and the plain request afterwards (`stale after settle: 0/20`).
3. In `playground/hmr`, editing a self-accepting module still hot-updates as before.

## Related Issue

Closes #23941
title: fix(hmr): invalidate module in `reloadModule` to discard in-flight transforms (fix #23941)

fixes #23930

In bundled mode, an asset imported from JS (`import url from './img.png'`) is loaded by the `vite:asset` `load` hook, but nothing registers the file for watching. `vite:asset` relies on the `originalFileName` it passes to `emitFile`, and Rolldown does not watch that file. So when the asset changes:

- no rebuild runs and `watchChange` never fires, so the cached entry in `assetCache` is never cleared
- later rebuilds (for example after editing the importer) reuse the old module, so the old hashed URL and content stay until the server restarts

The other ways of referencing an asset already call `this.addWatchFile` (`new URL(..., import.meta.url)` in `assetImportMetaUrl.ts`, CSS `url()` in `css.ts`, and `?raw` in the same `load` hook), which is why only plain imports were affected.

This PR calls `this.addWatchFile` for the asset file in the `load` hook when the environment is bundled (public files are skipped). This also fixes `vite build --watch`, which had the same problem: replacing an imported image did not trigger a rebuild.

### Tests

- Added `not inlined asset is up to date after a page reload` in `playground/hmr`. It fails without this change under `VITE_TEST_BUNDLED_DEV=1` (`expected '30' to be '150'`) and passes with it. It also passes in unbundled dev.
- `not inlined assets HMR` / `inlined assets HMR` now pass when run alone under bundled dev, but are still flaky when run after the earlier tests in the file, so I kept them as `bundledDevTodo` and updated the reason text.
- Ran `playground/hmr` (bundled dev x3, unbundled, build), `playground/assets` (bundled dev, build) and the `packages/vite` unit tests.

### Alternative

Fixing this in Rolldown so that `originalFileName` watches the file, as documented. This change doesn't conflict with that and matches what the other asset plugins do already.

### AI usage

Claude Code helped me with testing and information gathering. I reproduced the bug with a small script against the local build, traced it through `asset.ts`, and checked each test result with and without the change before keeping it.
title: fix(asset): watch imported assets in bundled mode

body:
## Description

Fixes a module runner regression where a package imported as a bare specifier entry (`runner.import('pkg')`) fails to re-import on `full-reload`. After the fix, `@vitejs/esm-external` keeps its bare url instead of being rewritten to `@vitejs/esm-external.mjs`, which could never be resolved again.

## Root cause

`EnvironmentModuleGraph._resolveUrl` appends the resolved id's extension to any url that differs from its resolved id, turning `pkg` into `pkg.js`. The module runner then stores that url and re-imports it on full reload, so `pkg.js` fails with `Failed to load url pkg.js ... Does the file exist?`.

The fix skips the extension rewrite when `bareImportRE.test(url)`. Bare specifiers stay untouched, while `/`-rooted urls, `./` urls, `file://` urls, and Windows drive paths follow the old path exactly as before. Callers through import analysis pass resolved-id-based urls starting with `/`, so they are not affected.

## Fix

- `packages/vite/src/node/server/moduleGraph.ts` — one condition in `_resolveUrl`; imports the existing `bareImportRE` from `../utils`.
- `packages/vite/src/node/ssr/runtime/__tests__/server-runtime.spec.ts` — new test `re-imports a bare specifier entry on full reload (#19975)`. It sends a real `full-reload` payload using the existing `@vitejs/esm-external` fixture and waits for a new module record. No mocks, no new files.

## Verification

- New test fails without the fix (`expected undefined to be defined`) and passes with it.
- Full unit suite: 73 files, 1090 passed, 3 skipped.
- `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck`, and `pnpm run format` followed by `git diff --exit-code` all pass.
- Extra: serve-mode playground groups `ssr`, `hmr` + `resolve`, and `hmr-ssr` pass.

## Related

This addresses the same root cause as open PR #22375 (fix(module-graph): keep bare-specifier urls intact), which has not been reviewed since May 2026. That PR guards with `url[0] === '/' || url[0] === '.'`, which also changes `file://` and drive-letter urls. Its test re-imports entry urls by hand rather than sending `full-reload`.

Closes #19975.

Ping @sapphi-red @bluwy — would love your take on this when you have a moment. No rush! 🙏
title: fix(module-runner): keep bare specifier entry urls intact (fix #19975)

body:
`build.write: false` is now applied in watch mode: it is passed to the watcher as `skipWrite: true`.

Refs #20412

The cause: in a normal build, Vite looks at `write` and calls `write()` or `generate()`. In watch mode, Rolldown's watcher writes the files, and Vite never passed `write: false` to it.

This doesn't fully close the issue. The issue author wanted to get the bundle with `event.result.generate()`, but Vite now uses Rolldown and this method doesn't exist there; `event.result` only has `close()`. So this can't be solved on the Vite side. But the main goal, getting the bundle in watch mode without writing to disk, is now possible with `write: false` + `generateBundle`. Also, the previously closed #23453 only delayed `close()`, which doesn't gain anything in Rolldown.

Behavior changes:
- With watch + `write: false`, nothing is written to disk anymore and `writeBundle` hooks don't run. This is already how `write: false` works without watch.
- In my comment on the issue I said I didn't touch `skipWrite` if it was set explicitly, but I changed this. Now nothing is written even with `write: false` + `skipWrite: false`, because otherwise the bundle was written but `outDir` wasn't emptied, so old files piled up.

I also added two tests. The `write: false` test fails without the fix; the `write: true` test is there to make sure nothing breaks.

I used AI while writing this change. But before the fix, I reproduced the problem myself and saw it happen. I confirmed that the cause was `write: false` not being passed on.
title: fix(build): respect `build.write: false` in watch mode

body:
When `server.headers` is configured, the dev server applies those headers (plus `ETag` and `Cache-Control`) on a module's first load but drops them on every load after. Dev modules are served `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so the browser revalidates on each reload and gets a `304 Not Modified`, and the 304 paths returned early without the headers the 200 applies. So a header like `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` or a CSP set via `server.headers` is there on a hard reload and silently gone on a normal reload. RFC 7232 also requires a 304 to carry the `ETag` and `Cache-Control` a 200 would.

The four dev-server 304 sites (`send`, the two transform shortcuts, and the bundled-dev memory files) now go through a shared `send304` helper that applies each response's own validators and configured headers. Tests cover each path and fail without the fix.
title: fix(server): keep configured headers and validators on 304 responses

## Summary

Fixes #23925

A module worker with a non-literal dynamic import gets `import { injectQuery } from "/@vite/client"` prepended by import analysis. That loads the full HMR client inside the worker, and it opens its own HMR socket. When a stylesheet linked from the page is edited, the worker's copy of the client receives the `css-update` and calls `document.querySelectorAll("link")`. A worker has no `document`, so this throws `ReferenceError: document is not defined` on every CSS edit.

## Root cause

The `update` case in `handleMessage` (`packages/vite/src/client/client.ts`) has a `js-update` branch that delegates to `hmrClient.queueUpdate`, but the `css-update` path directly accesses `document.querySelectorAll` without checking whether `document` exists. The rest of the client already guards DOM access with `hasDocument` (e.g. overlay, full-reload, error handling), but the CSS update path was missed.

## Changes

- Add a `typeof document === 'undefined'` guard at the top of the `css-update` path in `handleMessage`, so workers silently skip CSS link updates they cannot apply.

## Test plan

- [x] New e2e test in `playground/worker` that creates a module worker with a non-literal dynamic import (triggering `injectQuery` injection), edits a linked stylesheet, and verifies no `document is not defined` error is thrown
- [x] RED→GREEN verified: test fails without the guard (`worker unhandledrejection: document is not defined`), passes with it
- [x] All 21 worker tests pass (4 skipped)
- [x] All 60 HMR tests pass (2 skipped)
title: fix(client): skip css-update in workers without document

body:
fix #22078

Externalization decisions depend on where a package is imported from, but the current cache only uses the package ID. When the same ID resolves to different packages, the cached decision can incorrectly externalize linked source or inline a CommonJS dependency, depending on import order.

This change adds the directory `tryNodeResolve` resolves bare imports from to the cache key: the importer's directory if the importer exists on disk, otherwise `root`. That rule is now a helper (`getNodeResolveBasedir`) shared by both, so they stay in sync. The externalization resolver also gets its own `packageCache`.

Unlike #22080's file-level key, importers in the same directory share cached decisions. #22080 is slow mainly because this resolver had no package cache, so every new importer re-reads `package.json`. With a cache, both keys perform about the same.

### Validation

- The three new tests fail on `main` (a later call gets an earlier call's result) and pass with this change.
- With the reproduction, `b a` fails on `main` with `ReferenceError: module is not defined`, and `a b` externalizes `dep@2`. With this change, both orders match loading each package alone.

### Benchmark

Vite e954a9cda, Node v24.12.0, Apple M5; 2,000 modules across 100 folders, 10 bare imports per module. Median of five cold loads.

| Variant | Run 1 | Run 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | 745 ms | 671 ms |
| #22080 | 1710 ms | 1820 ms |
| Directory key only | 734 ms | 712 ms |
| #22080 + shared `config.packageCache` | 731 ms | 719 ms |
| This PR | 614 ms | 664 ms |

Only #22080 without a package cache is clearly slower; the other variants are within run-to-run noise of `main`.

Reproduction and benchmark: https://github.com/oyobbeb/vite-22078-repro

### Review notes

The dedicated `packageCache` is not cleared when a `package.json` changes, because the watcher only invalidates `config.packageCache`. `processedIds` was never cleared on `main` either, so this only affects (id, directory) pairs first seen after the change. I kept it separate because `config.packageCache` stores resolved entries without `isProduction` in the key, and `isProduction` is fixed to `false` here.

### AI assistance

AI tools assisted with the investigation, implementation, and tests. I read how `tryNodeResolve` picks its base directory, reviewed the diff, and chose this approach after comparing the variants above.
title: fix(ssr): cache externalization per importer directory (fix #22078)

body:
## Description

Refs #23907

When a file is deleted, `onFileDelete` only removed the module from its importees' `importers` sets, but left the module's `transformResult` (the transformed source code), `info`, and `meta` attached to the node. The nodes themselves are retained in all graph maps (`urlToModuleMap`, `idToModuleMap`, `fileToModulesMap`, `etagToModuleMap`) — this is intentional because the file-recreation recovery path (`handleHMRUpdate('create')` → `getModulesByFile(file)`) needs the node to still be present.

This causes two problems:

1. **Per-module memory growth**: the `transformResult` source code is retained for the life of the dev server. Files that are repeatedly created and deleted (renames, generated files, branch switches) accumulate stale transformed source.
2. **Stale node reuse**: when a deleted file is re-created, `_ensureEntryFromUrl` finds the stale node and returns it with its old `transformResult` still attached, instead of serving fresh content.

## Fix

In `onFileDelete`, for each module of the deleted file:
- clear `transformResult` via `updateModuleTransformResult(mod, null)` (also clears the stale `etagToModuleMap` entry — the previous direct assignment bypassed this cleanup)
- clear `info` and `meta`
- clear `importedModules` (after removing itself from each imported module's `importers`) to break outgoing references

**Module nodes are intentionally retained in all maps.** Removing them breaks the file-recreation recovery path: when a deleted file is recreated, the watcher fires a `create` event, `handleHMRUpdate('create')` calls `getModulesByFile(file)` to find the module and propagate restoration. If the node was removed during `delete` processing, `create` finds nothing and recovery HMR doesn't fire.

## Remaining limitation

Map sizes still grow with the number of distinct deleted file paths (one node per path). This PR clears the per-module data (the dominant memory cost for real-world source files) but does not remove the nodes themselves. Full graph-node cleanup would require a post-HMR-propagation cleanup hook and should be handled separately. See the [200-cycle reproduction comparison](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/23908#issuecomment-6495435780) for details.

## Tests

Five new unit tests in `moduleGraph.spec.ts`:
- `clears transform result and breaks outgoing references` — verifies transformResult/info/meta are cleared and importedModules is empty
- `reuses module node with cleared transform result after deletion` — verifies a re-created file reuses the same node but with `transformResult === null` (RED without the fix: stale transformResult is served)
- `keeps fileToModulesMap bounded on repeated create/delete cycles` — verifies the map doesn't grow beyond 1 entry for the same file path
- `clears stale ETag mapping on file delete` — verifies `etagToModuleMap` doesn't retain entries for deleted modules
- `clears transformResult for distinct deleted files` — verifies all modules for 5 distinct deleted files are cleaned

All 8 unit tests in the file pass, plus 71 server unit tests and 274 plugin unit tests with no regressions.
title: fix: clear stale module data on file delete (refs #23907)

### Description

Fixes #23807.

When an HTML `<link>` tag uses an `href` consisting only of a query string (e.g. `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="?md">`), `isExcludedUrl` does not check for `url[0] === '?'`. body:
### Description

When a Vite project root is located within an ancestor `.git` directory (for example, in git worktrees located under `.git/worktrees/<name>`), the default `server.fs.deny` rule (`'**/.git/**'`) matches all files under the root. This results in 403 Forbidden responses when serving files. Additionally, Chokidar ignores `'**/.git/**'`, which prevents file watching and causes HMR updates to be missed.

### Changes

- In `resolveServerOptions` (`packages/vite/src/node/server/index.ts`):
  - Check whether `resolvedRoot` contains an ancestor `.git` path component (`/(?:^|\/)\.git(?:$|\/)/.test(resolvedRoot)`).
  - When detected, scope the default `'**/.git/**'` deny entry to `${escapePath(resolvedRoot)}/**/.git/**`, preventing the ancestor `.git` directory from blocking project files while maintaining denial for `.git` directories located beneath the root. Sibling `.git` directories outside root remain restricted by `server.fs.allow`.
- In `resolveChokidarOptions` (`packages/vite/src/node/watch.ts`):
  - Accept `root?: string` as a parameter.

body:
### Description

When pre-bundling dependencies with Rolldown, entry chunk filenames can be disambiguated or suffixed with index numbers (for example, when multiple subpath exports resolve to modules that produce identical chunk names or on case-insensitive filesystems).

Previously, Vite indexed `depForEntryFileName` exclusively by `${flattenId(dep.id)}.js`. When an entry chunk was emitted under a disambiguated filename (e.g., `test_entry2.js`), `depForEntryFileName[chunk.fileName]` evaluated to `undefined`, triggering a fatal TypeError:
`Cannot destructure property 'exportsData' of depForEntryFileName[chunk.fileName] as it is undefined`.

This change resolves the matching `OptimizedDepInfo` by:
1. Checking `depForEntryFileName[chunk.fileName]`.
2. Falling back to `depForEntryFileName[`${chunk.name}.js`]`.
3. Falling back to the normalized filename without disambiguation suffixes.
4. Falling back to looking up `chunk.facadeModuleId` in a reverse map (`depForFacadeModuleId`) keyed by normalized `dep.src`.
5. Pointing `metadata.optimized[id].file` to the actual disambiguated chunk file path written to the cache directory.
6. Throwing an explicit descriptive error if an entry chunk cannot be resolved instead of encountering an uncaught destructuring TypeError.

Fixes #23757.

### Alternatives Explored

1. Customizing chunk file name formatting in Rolldown output options: discarded because disambiguation is an internal Rolldown/Rollup behavior for collision resolution and can also be affected by external filesystem semantics.
2. Only stripping numeric suffixes: insufficient when chunk names differ from entry filenames due to subpath alias structures. Falling back to `chunk.name` and `chunk.facadeModuleId` covers all chunk name variations.

### Additional Notes

A regression unit test has been added under `packages/vite/src/node/__tests__/optimizer/deconflictedEntryChunk.spec.ts` to verify that dependencies with conflicting entry chunk names optimize without runtime errors and register their emitted output paths accurately.

body:
### What is this PR solving?

In Vite 8 dev, an imported `.json` module is served with a full inline source map, and the SSR transform builds another one. Vite 7 does not generate any map for JSON.

Reproduction: https://stackblitz.com/github/wallynm/vite-json-sourcemap

To check it, run `npm run check`. The output compares Vite 8.3.5 and 7.3.7: on Vite 8 the JSON module is about 6x larger, with an inline source map and a large SSR source map; on Vite 7 there is none.

| | client module for a 2.1 MB JSON | inline map | SSR mappings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vite 7.3.7 | 2.3 MB | no | 0 |
| Vite 8.3.5 | 13.1 MB | yes | 5.6M chars |
| this PR | 2.3 MB | no | 0 |

In an SSR app (TanStack Start) this took the dev server from ~270 MB to ~1 GB RSS after a few edits of the file.

### Cause

In dev, `builtin:vite-json` runs through the JS plugin container and returns its map in rolldown's binding shape, `{ inner: { mappings: '' } }`. `_getCombinedSourcemap` only recognizes `{ mappings: '' }` as an empty map, so it returns `null`. With a `null` map, `send()` injects the high-resolution fallback map with the full source, and `ssrTransformScript` generates its own.

### Fix

Unwrap `{ inner }` when a transform result enters the sourcemap chain. The empty map is then recognized and no fallback map is generated. Build is not affected, since there the plugin runs inside rolldown.

### Alternatives

Unwrapping the map in rolldown's callable builtin plugin wrapper would fix it at the source, for any native plugin called from JS. I kept the change in Vite because the dev plugin container is the only consumer of that path today. Happy to move it if you prefer.

Related: #23549 and the open PRs #23561 / #23596 move dev source maps out of the response. They don't stop the map from being generated for JSON.

### Tests

- New test in `pluginContainer.spec.ts`: it fails without the fix (`null`) and passes with it (`{ mappings: '' }`).
- `playground/json` and `playground/js-sourcemap` pass in serve and build.

### AI usage

I used Claude (Claude Code) to investigate the memory growth, bisect it down to the sourcemap chain, and write the fix and the test.

I validated it myself before opening this PR:

- Reproduced the problem on a local replica of our production dev setup (TanStack Start with SSR, Vite 8), where a 2 MB JSON imported from `src/` took the dev server from ~270 MB to ~1 GB RSS, and confirmed the drop to ~400 MB with the same fix applied as a plugin.
- Reproduced it again in clean `create-vite` apps (vanilla and React) on macOS, on Linux (Docker) and on StackBlitz, comparing Vite 7.3.7 and 8.3.5.
- Traced the chain with `DEBUG=vite:sourcemap-combine` to confirm the `{ inner }` shape coming from `builtin:vite-json`.
- Ran the new test without and with the fix, the full unit suite, and the `json` and `js-sourcemap` playgrounds in serve and build.

I reviewed the diff line by line and can explain the change.
title: fix(dev): keep empty sourcemap from native plugins

body:
## Description

Fix #23880.

The Rolldown-based dependency scanner tree-shakes unreferenced functions before collecting dynamic imports. A `import()` that is only reachable through such a function — for example an event handler in a single-file component that is only used by the template, which the scanner only sees as an unreferenced function in the `<script>` block — is therefore not crawled. Its dependencies are not pre-bundled at startup and are only discovered when the browser first requests them, triggering `optimized dependencies changed. reloading`.

The scanner is a crawl: tree-shaking is counterproductive here and can only hide dependencies. The esbuild scanner in Vite 7 never tree-shook. This disables tree-shaking for the scan stage, restoring the previous behavior.

## Verification

- New regression test in `packages/vite/src/node/__tests__/scan.spec.ts` with a fixture where an unreferenced function contains a dynamic `import()`: fails without the fix (`deps` is empty), passes with it.
- `pnpm run test-unit` (1072 passed)
- `pnpm run typecheck`
title: fix(optimizer): crawl dynamic imports in unreferenced code during dep scan

body:
An imported but unused lazy asset loader can leave its external asset in the build even after its JavaScript is removed. This change marks build assets as conditional and retains them when surviving JavaScript, CSS, HTML or an explicit asset entry owns a reference. Used loaders keep their original URL behavior and asset bytes.

This draft depends on the proposed Rolldown `needsCodeReference` and `referenceFile` APIs. Rolldown's native file-URL handling retains JavaScript references; Vite records ownership when rendering its existing CSS/HTML/JavaScript asset placeholders and for explicit asset entries. Bundled development emission remains unconditional. Base paths, query/hash processing, inline policy and content deduplication are unchanged.

The Rolldown approach is being discussed in [rolldown/rolldown#10064](https://github.com/rolldown/rolldown/issues/10064#issuecomment-6358025096); API agreement and a supporting release are prerequisites. The change requires matching native Rolldown and JavaScript support. It must not merge against a released Rolldown version that lacks these APIs. Once a supporting Rolldown release exists, this draft needs the corresponding dependency and lockfile update; no hypothetical version is specified here.

Tests are enrolled in `packages/vite/src/node/__tests__/asset-ownership.spec.js` and the existing assets playground. The playground imports a dead loader and exposes a live loader using two small WASM fixtures. It asserts no unused asset, exactly one used asset and successful retrieval of the original used bytes. Unit controls cover CSS splitting, query/hash/base handling, HTML ownership, public files, explicit entries, manifest visibility, late ownership, duplicate ownership and multiple outputs.

Validation on Linux x64 GNU with Node 22.23.2, patched Vite 8.3.4 and a matching optimized Rolldown 1.2.14 prototype:

- Normal upstream unit harness: 15 ownership tests passed.
- Selected assets, HTML and CSS-code-split playground build suites: 304 tests passed, 16 existing skips; 9 spec files passed and 1 was skipped. The new regression passed alone and in the selected suite. Existing asset build-watch tests also passed.
- Browser qualification used cached Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (revision 1248) via an execution-only launch override. Playwright 1.63.0 expects revision 1243, which was not used. The override is not part of this patch.
- A separate clean-install consumer check with a packaged component library reproduced the original unused 466,610-byte WASM and emitted no assets with the patched unused loader. The used loader emitted one byte-identical WASM, made no WASM request before activation, then fetched it once and successfully highlighted code without page errors.
- The dependent Rolldown regression fails against its original binding with one unwanted asset versus zero expected, and passes against the candidate.

Limits: full upstream suites and other platforms remain unqualified. Experimental incremental retention is conservative; this does not claim complete Vite HMR or arbitrary post-minifier liveness. Updating a project's tooling does not fix other consumers that continue using older bundler versions.

Source base: [Vite b6c20f6](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/tree/b6c20f6a8126d8561891e5fb9368e8fc9da37538). Related existing code: [asset plugin](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/b6c20f6a8126d8561891e5fb9368e8fc9da37538/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/asset.ts), [CSS plugin](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/b6c20f6a8126d8561891e5fb9368e8fc9da37538/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/css.ts), [HTML plugin](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/b6c20f6a8126d8561891e5fb9368e8fc9da37538/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/html.ts), [playground harness](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/b6c20f6a8126d8561891e5fb9368e8fc9da37538/vitest.config.e2e.ts).

Related work: [#19949](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/19949) and [#9073](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/9073) report assets retained after their JavaScript or CSS reference disappears. The closed, unmerged [#20778](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/20778) discussed conditional emission after blanket asset deletion was rejected because plugin-owned assets must be preserved. This proposal records opt-in ownership rather than deleting arbitrary plugin assets. The merged worker-specific [#22473](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/22473) uses worker bundle reachability and remains unchanged. These are related cases, not claims that their original reproductions have been qualified; references removed by later render/minifier hooks can still leave retained assets.

AI assistance was used for implementation, technical review, and test preparation. The technical review checked conditional and unconditional ownership, late and duplicate owners, passive filename lookup, CSS/HTML/entry ownership, and retained asset bytes. This contribution is submitted by `aceshooting`; the validation and remaining limits are listed above.
title: feat(asset): omit unreferenced build assets

body:
## Description

`bundleWorkerEntry` only checked the cache for worker bundles that had already finished. When two workers started the same nested worker while the first build of it was still in flight, both calls missed the cache and an identical second build was started (#23848). In apps with many workers this multiplies build work; output is byte-identical.

This PR keeps the in-flight build in a pending map on `WorkerOutputCache`, so concurrent requests for the same worker input await the running build instead of starting a duplicate. The circular-import check still runs before the pending lookup, so a worker importing itself still fails fast instead of waiting on its own build.

Fixes #23848

## Reproduction / validation

- Repro from the issue (two parents `start-a.js` / `start-b.js` both spawn a nested worker over an identical `shared.js`): before the fix the worker-plugin log shows `bundling worker: shared.js` twice on every run; after the fix it appears once, and only one `shared-*.js` chunk is built.
- Added a regression test: `playground/worker/__tests__/nested-dedupe/worker-nested-dedupe.spec.ts` builds the two-parents-one-nested-worker fixture and asserts `shared.js` is bundled exactly once. It fails on the unpatched build and passes with this change.
- `pnpm build` (rolldown + `tsc --project tsconfig.check.json`) passes.

Prepared with AI assistance.
